Step 3:  The problem states that 437 residents own exactly two of these items, and 234 residents own all four items. We can use the principle of inclusion-exclusion to solve this problem.

Step 4:  According to the principle of inclusion-exclusion, the total number of residents who own at least one of the items can be calculated as: |D ∪ G ∪ S ∪ C| = |D| + |G| + |S| + |C| - |D ∩ G| - |D ∩ S| - |D ∩ C| - |G ∩ S| - |G ∩ C| - |S ∩ C| + |D ∩ G ∩ S| + |D ∩ G ∩ C| + |D ∩ S ∩ C| + |G ∩ S ∩ C| - |D ∩ G ∩ S ∩ C|.

Step 6:  Now, we can use the principle of inclusion-exclusion to find the value of |D ∩ G ∩ S ∩ C|.

Step 7:  By rearranging the equation, we get: |D ∩ G ∩ S ∩ C| = |D ∪ G ∪ S ∪ C| - |D| - |G| - |S| - |C| + |D ∩ G| + |D ∩ S| + |D ∩ C| + |G ∩ S| + |G ∩ C| + |S ∩ C|.

Step 8:  Substituting the given values, we get: |D ∩ G ∩ S ∩ C| = 900 - 195 - 367 - 562 - 900 + 437 + 3*234.
